blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one. We organize the evaluation around model quality, drafting and verification costs, and deployment under constrained memory. We also describe a decision-model variant that generates answers to related questions in one denoising pass. On an internal set of 500 groups, joint prediction raises question accuracy from 90.37% to 93.88% and all-correct group accuracy from 65.4% to 77.0%.

Clover将Gated Delta Networks通过将以前生成的内存与当前块内的双向软马克思注意力相结合来进行阻断扩散. 历史记忆读出器在共享软max中与当前块符号竞争,具有可学习的块大小校准以及单独零初始化的右文本折叠分支. blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer a different route to language generation:
reconstructing sequences through iterative denoising, with multiple tokens
predicted in parallel. This formulation connects flexible generation order
with the prospect of efficient inference. Progress in diffusion formulations,
model scaling, and decoding has brought DLMs from specialized text-generation
settings to increasingly capable general-purpose models. The next step is to
translate these advances into strong performance and practical efficiency
across demanding applications.

blocks.en: 2.2 Self-speculative decoding

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by verifying
multiple draft tokens in a single target-model pass [ 5 , 28 ] .
Recently, diffusion language models offer a natural drafting mechanism through
parallel block prediction, as demonstrated by
DFlash [ 7 ] and DFlash 2 [ 24 ] .
Self-speculative decoding integrates
these roles within the same model: diffusion-style block prediction supplies
candidate tokens, and autoregressive verification determines which prefix can
be committed. NVIDIA’s Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion supports autoregressive,
diffusion, and self-speculation decoding within one
model [ 15 ] .

Context parallelism shards a sequence across devices, but the required
communication differs by mixer. Full-attention layers keep local queries
and gather and reorder K/V. BD-GDN supports either a Ulysses
sequence-to-head transpose [ 25 ] or recurrent-state
propagation using the context-parallel implementation in Flash Linear
Attention (FLA) 1 1 1 https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/fla/ops/cp [ 59 ] , which we refer

consistent across ranks and pipeline stages processing the same example.

Table 2 shows that Clover sustains high committed-token
yields across all three workloads, exceeding DFlash 2 in tokens committed per
verification round. On MATH-500, however, its higher drafting cost offsets
this advantage, resulting in lower decode throughput than DFlash 2. On agent
replay and daily chat, Clover achieves both higher committed-token yields and
higher throughput. We attribute this advantage to Clover’s drafting capability developing alongside the model throughout training. In contrast, methods such as DFlash train a separate lightweight drafter on target-generated responses over a selected prompt distribution, which may not cover the full range of workloads supported by the target. Expanding training data can improve coverage, but the drafter’s limited capacity may still constrain how well it captures the target’s behavior across workloads.
These results highlight the importance of both draft cost and workload coverage when translating speculative progress into speed.

Expert placement strongly affects hybrid execution because CPU expert
computation is slower and can dominate generation time. We use routing
statistics from mathematical tasks to place frequently used experts on the
GPU and less frequently used experts on the CPU, reducing CPU computation

computation. These results highlight the value of matching expert placement
to workload demand alongside decoding optimization.

blocks.en: 5 Clover Decision Model
blocks.zh: 5 克洛弗决定模型

blocks.en:
Human decision-making is often described in terms of fast, intuitive
System 1 thinking and slower, deliberate System 2 reasoning.
Drawing on this distinction, Jev, a commercial model from TypeSafe AI,
targets fast, structured decisions that software can use
directly [ 1 ] .
This motivates the Clover decision model: we use block diffusion to produce
related judgments jointly in a single denoising pass, combining fast response
with the ability to share information across decisions.

questions while reading all answers in one denoising pass. Figure 5 compares it with sequential and parallel independent calls under the same

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, a 35B-total, 3B-active mixture-of-experts diffusion language
model built around a bidirectional adaptation of Gated Delta Networks. Its
architecture combines recurrent historical memory, selective interactions
within the current block, learnable block-size calibration, and bidirectional
local features. The benchmark results show a consistent lead across the evaluated agent
metrics alongside competitive general capabilities, with opportunities for
further improvement in knowledge and mathematics.
Quantized deployment offers a further direction
for studying this architecture under memory constraints. Our decision-model
results additionally suggest that jointly generating related answers can
improve the correctness of a complete set of judgments.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了Clover-35B-A3B-Preview,一种35B-总计,3B-活性混合专家传播语言.
Gated Delta Networks的双向改造模型。 内容
结构结合了反复出现的历史记忆,选择性互动
在当前块内,可学习块大小校准,双向
当地特色。 基准结果显示,在被评价的代理人中,领先一致
衡量标准与具有竞争力的一般能力并列,
进一步提高知识和数学水平。
量化部署提供了进一步的方向
用于在记忆限制下研究此架构. 我们的决定模式
成果还表明,联合产生相关答案可以
提高一整套判决的正确性。

blocks.en:
The next priorities are to further reduce latency, characterize the
quality–latency trade-off under matched evaluation conditions, and strengthen
quantized deployment. We are also extending Clover toward multimodal
capabilities, informed by Dream-VL and Dream-VLA work on
vision-language understanding and robotic action modeling [ 63 ] , and extending the context length.
